newsitem.title: UK: Pro-EU British party attacks common fish policy.
newsitem.headline: Pro-EU British party attacks common fish policy.

text.p: Britain's most pro-European political party on Wednesday declared the bloc's Common Fisheries Policy was "deeply flawed" and demanded it should be scrapped and control taken away from Brussels.
Delegates to the annual conference of the minority Liberal Democrats called for a new policy under which power would be handed back to fishermen and scientists in regions of the EU.

The proposed new policy would bring an end to the current practice where Spanish-owned trawlers fish close to Britain's coast after buying part of the quota for catching fish supposed to be given to British boats.
The Conservative government has protested at this "quota hopping" and called for it to be discussed at the EU's intergovernmental conference which is revising the bloc's institutions.

Calling for the change, European Parliament member Robin Teverson said the current Brussels-managed policy was "extravagant in the way it destroys our fish stocks and menaces the future of our coastal communities".
Teverson said despite the party's pro-EU stance it would not be silent where it believed Brussels had got things wrong. "And here European policy is deeply flawed," he said.
Liberal Democrat member of parliament Jim Wallace said the change would also lead to better conservation of fish stocks.

"By giving fishermen responsibility for their own area, we give them a reason to manage stocks responsibly. Just as no farmer would slaughter all his cattle, no fisherman is going to fish his stocks to extinction," he said.
